newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican labor baron, 96, hospitalized again.
newsitem.headline: Mexican labor baron, 96, hospitalized again.

text.p: Fidel Velazquez, the 96-year-old head of Mexico's largest labour confederation, was hospitalized on Monday with an intestinal infection, his second illness in five months, his doctor said.
Salomon Jasqui told Reuters that Velazquez would stay in the hospital three or for days for a checkup.
"It's nothing serious," Jasqui said. "He's being treated intravenously with serum and antibiotics. I'm going to take advantage of this to give him a checkup."

Velazquez, who as the unchallenged leader of the Mexican Workers Confederation (CTM) is Mexico's most powerful labour baron and a pillar of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), was last hospitalized in October with pneumonia.
In recent public appearances he has looked weak, having trouble holding his head up and speaking.
But he remains a combative stalwart of his party, and he recently threatened to expel members of the six million-strong CTM if they failed to vote for the PRI in mid-term elections on July 6.
For half a century as Mexico's top union leader, Velazquez has managed to keep a lid on labour unrest, even though for the last two decades real wages have fallen.
